"Create a magical fantasy RPG inspired by the Harry Potter universe, combining wand crafting, magical education, spell collecting and wizard dueling.

You play as a young aspiring wizard who starts with a basic wand and gradually becomes a legendary wandmaker and duelist.

1. Wand Crafting System

- Collect different magical woods, cores and rare materials.
- Craft wands with different lengths, flexibility, magical properties and appearances.
- Experiment with combinations of wood and cores to discover unique wand abilities.
- Every wand has different strengths, weaknesses and spell compatibility.
- Upgrade, customize and sell wands to other witches and wizards.
- Discover legendary and extremely rare wand combinations.

2. Spell Learning @COMMENT_BODY@ Magic School

- Attend magical lessons to unlock different spell categories.
- Learn spells through interactive challenges and practice.
- Categories include offensive, defensive, healing, elemental, transformation and forbidden magic.
- Master spells to unlock stronger versions and special abilities.
- Different wands can improve certain spell categories or completely change how spells behave.

3. Wizard Dueling

- Real-time magical dueling with other students, teachers, monsters and powerful wizards.
- Use combinations of spells, defensive shields, dodging and counterattacks.
- Build your own fighting style depending on your wand and learned spells.
- Competitive dueling tournaments with rankings and rewards.
- Boss battles against legendary dark wizards.

4. Exploration @COMMENT_BODY@ Progression

- Explore a massive magical world with enchanted forests, ancient ruins, hidden caves and magical villages.
- Discover rare wand ingredients, magical creatures and secret spells.
- Complete quests, challenges and magical examinations.
- Unlock new locations as your magical reputation increases.

5. Economy @COMMENT_BODY@ Collection

- Open your own wand shop and become a respected wandmaker.
- Sell custom-crafted wands to NPCs with different magical personalities and preferences.
- Build a collection of rare wands, magical creatures, ingredients and spellbooks.
- Reinvest earnings into better crafting equipment and rare materials.

Visual style: Beautiful 3D fantasy world, atmospheric magical environments, detailed wand designs, spectacular spell effects and immersive real-time combat.

Main objective: Become the greatest wandmaker and most powerful duelist in the magical world. Your wand, your spells and your choices determine your legacy.

---

---
name: load-sketchfab-threejs
description: Find low-resource downloadable Sketchfab models, preserve attribution, inspect and normalize GLB materials, load assets and animation clips with official Three.js GLTFLoader and PlayCanvas Container loaders, and prove geometry, animation, and material fidelity in a real browser. Use for Sketchfab search/download, Three.js or PlayCanvas GLB integration, missing or incorrect textures/materials/animations, legacy glTF extensions, camera-framing defects, or browser-visible A/B verification.
---

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
display

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable magical fantasy RPG featuring wand crafting, magical lessons and spell collecting, real-time duels, exploration, progression, and a wand shop.
- Deliver a polished 3D presentation and verify the game in-browser with a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Include customizable wands and materials, six spell categories, duels and tournaments, explorable locations, quests, economy, collection, and progression.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; infer content for placeholder headings and briefly note assumptions at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Created an original magical setting, Aurelian Academy and Emberfall, rather than using named Harry Potter characters or locations.
- Use Three.js with procedural geometry, original game content, and Vite.
- No explicit decisions recorded for the placeholder headings; the game data provides inferred lessons, exploration, quests, and economy.

## Work State
### Completed
- Established a Vite/Three.js project with `package.json`, dependencies, and a game UI shell in `index.html` and `src/style.css`.
- Added extensive original game data for wands, cores, materials, recipes, spells, lessons, enemies, quests, customers, upgrades, zones, and achievements in `src/data.js`.
- Implemented wand stat calculation, rarity, affinities, sales evaluation, and wand SVG illustrations in `src/crafting.js`.
- Implemented game state, progression, quests, crafting, sales, upgrades, inventory, and persistence in `src/game.js`.
- Added procedural wizard characters and animations in `src/character.js`.
- Added world utilities and procedural environment content across `src/worldkit.js`, `src/sites.js`, `src/sites2.js`, and `src/world.js`.
- Added spell visual effects and a duelling arena in `src/effects.js`.

### Active
- Finish the playable game by implementing UI/gameplay orchestration, spellcasting, movement, interaction, lessons, shop, duels, and save/load flows.

- `src/effects.js` may have runtime/API issues that need testing; the effects and arena implementation has not yet been verified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable magical fantasy RPG with wand crafting, lessons and spell collecting, exploration, progression, a shop, real-time duels, and tournaments.
- Deliver a polished 3D presentation and verify it in-browser with a current small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Include customizable wands and materials, six spell categories, duels and tournaments, explorable locations, quests, economy, collection, and progression.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; infer content for placeholder headings and briefly note assumptions at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use an original setting, Aurelian Academy and Emberfall, rather than named Harry Potter characters or locations.
- Use Three.js, procedural geometry, original game content, and Vite.

## Work State
### Completed
- Set up the Vite/Three.js project, game UI shell, styling, content data, crafting, game state, procedural characters and environments, and spell effects/arena.
- Added procedural WebAudio effects in `src/audio.js`.
- Added panel rendering for crafting, spells/lessons, shop, journal, atlas, character, and duels in `src/panels.js`.
- Added UI handling for panels, crafting, lessons, dialogue, challenges, HUD, and minimap in `src/ui.js`.
- Added real-time duel logic, movement, spellcasting, enemy AI, projectiles, status effects, and duel outcomes in `src/duel.js`.
- Corrected the Spire arena opacity update to write to the shader uniform in `src/effects.js`.

### Active
- Integrate the UI and duel modules with the game entry point, world, player controls, and `index.html`.
- Build and run the game, resolve runtime/API issues, exercise gameplay flows, and verify with the requested latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` is still missing, although `index.html` references it; the game is not yet runnable end-to-end.
- Newly added modules have only had syntax checks (`node --check ui.js`, `panels.js`, `effects.js`); no full build or browser verification has been done.

## Next Move
1. Inspect current `index.html`, `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and exports/APIs in the new modules; implement `src/main.js` and connect movement, interactions, spellcasting, UI actions, and duel lifecycle.
2. Run `npm run build`, start the Vite app, fix compile/runtime issues, and test core progression and combat.
3. Save and inspect one current JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px.
4. Summarize the finished gameplay and briefly state inferred assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI structure; entry point expects `/src/main.js`.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.
- `src/ui.js`: UI/controller and player-facing action hooks.
- `src/panels.js`: Game panel renderers.
- `src/duel.js`: Real-time duel simulation.
- `src/audio.js`: Procedural WebAudio effects.
- `src/game.js`: State, progression, quests, crafting, sales, upgrades, inventory, and persistence.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural world, NPCs, nodes, interactables, and collisions.
- `src/effects.js`: Spell effects and duel arena.
- `src/data.js`: Game content and progression definitions.
- `src/crafting.js`: Wand creation, stats, recipes, sales, and SVG rendering.
- `src/character.js`: Procedural wizard models and animations.
- `src/style.css`: Game interface styling.
- `src/sites.js`, `src/sites2.js`, `src/worldkit.js`: Procedural environments and world utilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no commit or push was recorded.
- `src/ui.js` exposes hooks through `ui.actions`; the missing entry point must wire them to the world, audio, and duel system.
- `src/effects.js` and `src/duel.js` have not been runtime-tested; inspect for Three.js API or lifecycle issues during integration.
